summary: Focused re-test of the anchor/backup/certificate flow on web Evidence Locker after main agent's readFileBytes() fix in evidenceBackup.ts. Result: the ORIGINAL bug ('this.validatePath is not a function') is confirmed fixed — that exact error no longer occurs. However, the flow is STILL completely broken on web with a NEW error at the exact same call site, so the end-user-visible outcome is unchanged: Anchor never succeeds, and Backup/Certificate buttons (gated on anchor existing) never appear.

integration_issues.flow: Evidence Locker — Anchor & verify (needs signal) on web
integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL (NOT fixed, regression of the same symptom with a new root cause): After tapping 'Anchor & verify' -> 'Skip' on the location dialog, evidence-status now shows: 'The method or property expo-file-system.readAsStringAsync is not available on web, are you sure you've linked all the native dependencies properly?' instead of the old validatePath error. Root cause: the new readFileBytes() web branch calls `FileSystem.readAsStringAsync()` from `expo-file-system/legacy`, but on web this legacy module resolves to `ExponentFileSystemShim` (node_modules/expo-file-system/src/legacy/ExponentFileSystemShim.ts) — a bare class exposing ONLY documentDirectory/cacheDirectory/bundleDirectory, with NO readAsStringAsync implementation at all. Every legacy FileSystem.readAsStringAsync call on web in this installed expo-file-system version (~19.0.23) throws UnavailabilityError unconditionally, regardless of the URI passed. On top of that, item.uri is intentionally blank ('') on web for stored evidence items (see evidenceStore.web.ts — plaintext/ciphertext is only ever exposed as a transient blob: URL via getDecryptedTempUri(), never as item.uri) so even a working readAsStringAsync would have nothing valid to read from item.uri directly. Net result: Anchor is still 100% non-functional on web; Backup and Certificate buttons are still unreachable (same blocked state as the prior test iteration, just a different error string).

react_native_issues.issue: No red-screen crash — the thrown error is caught in evidence-locker.tsx's doAnchor() try/catch and surfaced gracefully as status text. This part of the error handling is solid; only the underlying byte-read implementation is broken on web.

action_items: CRITICAL — the readFileBytes() web branch must NOT use expo-file-system (legacy or new File API) at all — this installed version's legacy module is fully unimplemented/shimmed on web (confirmed via node_modules/expo-file-system/src/legacy/ExponentFileSystemShim.ts, which has zero methods). Use the browser-native `fetch(uri).then(r => r.arrayBuffer())` -> `new Uint8Array(buf)` pattern instead (same technique evidenceStore.web.ts already uses internally for blob handling).

CRITICAL — item.uri is blank ('') for web RecordingItem rows (by design, to avoid exposing ciphertext/plaintext paths). anchorItem() must first call getDecryptedTempUri(scope, item) to obtain a real decryptable blob: URL before it can read any bytes to hash on web — reading item.uri directly will never work on web regardless of which file API is used.

Once fixed, also verify backupItem()'s existing isWeb branch (lines ~93-99 in evidenceBackup.ts, also using FileSystem.readAsStringAsync on item.uri) — it has the exact same two bugs (broken legacy API + blank item.uri) and was never actually runtime-exercised in any prior test because Anchor always failed first and hid the Backup button. Do not assume it works just because anchor gets fixed — retest backup explicitly once anchor succeeds.
Certificate export (handleCertificate) was also not reachable/testable this run since it's gated on manifestMap[item.id]?.anchor existing — same blocker, retest once anchor truly works on web.
critical_code_review_comments: evidenceBackup.ts's readFileBytes() web branch is architecturally unsound for two independent reasons (broken legacy FileSystem on web + blank item.uri on web) — this wasn't a one-line fix, the whole web byte-read strategy needs to change to fetch()+getDecryptedTempUri() rather than any expo-file-system call.

Good defensive coding confirmed: errors from anchorItem() are caught and shown as readable status text rather than crashing the app (no red screen), which made this bug easy to diagnose from the UI alone.

seed_data_creation: One audio recording was created via the UI during this test session (ephemeral, stored only in the browser's IndexedDB for this test session/profile — not persisted to any backend/Mongo, auto-discarded when the browser context closed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Onboarding sequence needed before reaching /women/evidence-locker on a fresh browser profile: 1) consent screen (consent-age-adult -> consent-terms-checkbox -> consent-data-checkbox -> consent-continue-button), 2) login screen -> continue-as-guest-button, 3) this redirects back to consent?mode=update ONE more time — repeat step 1 again, 4) lands on /home as guest — THEN navigate directly to /women/evidence-locker again (first attempt right after guest redirects to /home, not the locker). PIN gate: fill evidence-pin-input with any 4-digit PIN, submit, then fill the SAME PIN again for confirm step, submit. This full sequence must be scripted in ONE browser_automation call since every call is a fresh profile. Do not re-test PIN/record/photo/video/share/delete — those were confirmed passing in iteration_26/27 and are unaffected by this change.
rca_of_issue: Main agent's fix (Platform-branched readFileBytes() helper) correctly solved the originally-reported symptom (new File(uri).bytes() throwing validatePath-is-not-a-function on web) by routing web reads through `expo-file-system/legacy`'s FileSystem.readAsStringAsync + atob() instead. However, this substituted one broken API for another: this installed expo-file-system version's legacy module has NO web implementation at all (ExponentFileSystemShim.ts on web exposes only 3 null directory constants, zero methods — readAsStringAsync, getInfoAsync, etc. all throw UnavailabilityError unconditionally on web). Separately, even a working readAsStringAsync would fail here because RecordingItem.uri is intentionally left as an empty string for web-stored items (evidenceStore.web.ts keeps plaintext/ciphertext only in an IndexedDB Blob, never as a file:// URI) — the only way to get a readable URI on web is via the existing getDecryptedTempUri(scope, item) helper which produces a temporary blob: URL. Reproduction: on web, create any audio recording, tap 'Anchor & verify' -> 'Skip', observe evidence-status text changes from 'Saved on this device...' to the new UnavailabilityError message; recording-vault-status-* stays 'Not anchored yet'; no backup/certificate buttons ever render. Suggested complete fix: readFileBytes() web branch should call `const blobUri = await getDecryptedTempUri(scope, item); const buf = await (await fetch(blobUri)).arrayBuffer(); const bytes = new Uint8Array(buf); releaseDecryptedTempUri(blobUri, true); return bytes;` (adjusting for whatever the real decrypt helper's exact signature/import path is in evidenceStore vs evidenceStore.web) — this avoids expo-file-system on web entirely and correctly sources plaintext bytes from the existing decrypt-on-demand mechanism already used for preview/play/share.
